differential.name: Diabetic kidney disease (diabetic nephropathy)
differential.rationale: Long‑standing prediabetes/early type 2 diabetes with microalbuminuria and CKD‑GFR ≈30 mL/min strongly suggest diabetic nephropathy as primary etiology.

differential.name: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis
differential.rationale: Chronic essential hypertension in a 40‑year‑old with progressive CKD and modest proteinuria can cause arteriolar sclerosis leading to reduced GFR.

differential.name: IgA nephropathy (primary chronic glomerulonephritis)
differential.rationale: Presents with slowly progressive CKD in young adults; absence of overt diabetes control makes it a secondary consideration.

differential.name: Obstructive uropathy (e.g., chronic kidney stone disease)
differential.rationale: Can cause CKD with elevated creatinine; no imaging data but must be excluded given CKD severity.

differential.name: NSAID‑induced chronic interstitial nephritis
differential.rationale: Chronic analgesic use can lead to interstitial fibrosis and CKD; plausible given possible self‑medication for stress‑related pain.
